title: Bold Words in String
statement: You are given a list of keywords `words` and a string `s`. A character of `s` must be shown in bold when it lies inside at least one occurrence of some keyword in `s` (occurrences may overlap one another). Return `s` with bold markup inserted: an opening tag `` and a closing tag `` around the bold characters, using as few tags as possible. In other words, every maximal block of consecutive bold characters is wrapped in exactly one `...` pair, so occurrences that overlap or touch end to end share a single pair, and characters that are not bold are copied unchanged. If no keyword occurs, return `s` as it is.
constraints: s and every words[i] contain only lowercase English letters
notes: ## Intuition Whether a character ends up bold depends only on whether some keyword occurrence covers it, not on which one. So first mark every covered position in a boolean array, then build the answer in one pass: a bold block starts where a marked character follows an unmarked one (or the start), and ends where a marked character is followed by an unmarked one (or the end). Overlapping and touching occurrences automatically merge into one block, which is exactly the "fewest tags" requirement. A brute force could test every substring of length up to 10 against a set of the keywords and merge the found intervals; marking is simpler. ## Approach 1. Create `bold`, one `false` per character of `s`. 2. For each `word`, find every occurrence with `indexOf`, restarting one position after the previous `start` so overlapping occurrences are found too. 3. Mark the `word.length` positions of each occurrence as bold. 4. Walk `s`: before a bold character whose left neighbour is not bold, append ``; append the character; after a bold character whose right neighbour is not bold, append ``. ## Example 1, step by step `words = ["ab","bc"]`, `s = "aabcd"`. `"ab"` occurs at index 1, marking positions 1 and 2; `"bc"` occurs at index 2, marking 2 and 3. So `bold = [F, T, T, T, F]`. Building: `"a"` is plain; index 1 starts a block, giving `"aa"`; indices 2 and 3 add `"bc"`, and index 3 ends the block with ``; `"d"` is plain. The result is `"aabcd"`. ## Complexity - Time: O(W · n · L) where W is the number of keywords, n = `s.length` and L the longest keyword: each search and each marking is bounded by n · L per keyword. - Space: O(n) for `bold` and the output. ## Pitfalls - Restart the search at `start + 1`, not `start + word.length`, or overlapping occurrences such as `"aa"` in `"aaa"` are missed. - Adjacent blocks must merge: `"ab"` and `"cd"` in `"abcd"` give `abcd`, not two tag pairs. - Guard the neighbour checks at the ends of the string (`i === 0` and `i === s.length - 1`). ## Variables | Name | Meaning | |---|---| | `bold` | `bold[i]` is true when some keyword occurrence covers `s[i]` | | `word` | the keyword being searched for | | `start` | index of the current occurrence of `word`, or -1 when none is left | | `result` | the string being built with tags | | `i` | the position being marked or copied |

narration.2: One flag per character records whether that character must be bold.
narration.3: Handle each keyword separately; the flags combine all of them.
narration.4: Find the first place this keyword occurs.
narration.5: Repeat for every occurrence until indexOf reports none.
narration.6: Visit each character this occurrence covers...
narration.9: Look again one step further on, so overlapping occurrences are not skipped.
narration.12: Build the answer from left to right.
narration.13: Walk over every character of s.
narration.14: A bold character with no bold character before it starts a new block.
narration.15: Open the block with a tag.
narration.18: A bold character with no bold character after it ends the block.
narration.22: Return the string with the fewest tags needed.
